name: Workplace registration and incident register service under the OSH Act
buyer: Small workplaces, workshops and premises needing an OSH certificate
trigger: Occupational Safety and Health Act 2006: workplace registration with the MGLSD Commissioner, renewable every 3 years (secondary source), incident register and inspection checklist; occupying a workplace without a certificate is an offence
evidence: https://bills.parliament.ug/attachments/Laws of Uganda (Acts) - THE OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH ACT, 2006.pdf; https://www.kaa.co.ug/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/KAA-workplace-registered-compliant.pdf
unchecked: Renewal interval confirmed only by a law-firm article; any lift, boiler or pressure-vessel examination schedule not found; generic compliance risk; enforcement intensity; online registration

first_check.duty: OSH Act Cap. 231 (2006): workplaces must register with the MGLSD Commissioner, and occupying one without a certificate is an offence. A law firm and a ministry speech (seen only as a search snippet; the PDF returned 404) say the certificate is renewable every 3 years. The OSH (Amendment) Act No. 20 of 2025, in force from 25 July 2025, extends the Act to all workplaces (the earlier 20-employee limit is repealed). Per search summaries it adds health surveillance plans submitted to the Commissioner and mandatory training or certification for machinery operators. Penalty amounts and safety committee thresholds were not reached, because the KTA alert PDF could not be decoded. No lift, boiler or pressure-vessel examination schedule was found.
first_check.market: Not confirmed. UBOS has published the 2019/20 Census of Business Establishments report, but I did not get its totals. The 2001/02 census listed about 160,000 or more fixed-premise establishments, mostly with fewer than 5 employees. The 2009/10 Uganda Business Inquiry put 96% of establishments in the informal economy. Since the 2025 amendment, all workplaces are in scope in principle, which is likely hundreds of thousands, but formal firms that can pay are a much smaller group. The number of registered workplaces was not found.
first_check.competitor: The free state portal OSHMIS (oshmis.mglsd.go.ug, cited in a ministry speech) handles online registration and certificates. Per a 2022 Monitor article, the ministry's online system also lets workplaces report problems. I found no commercial Ugandan OSH compliance software. The only local efforts are the UNCST-listed "OSH Tracking and Measurement System" (a prototype), Kashari Consults' digital OSH compliance system (in development, per VC4A) and a Makerere research prototype for construction. There are generic international apps such as OHS Assist. Local OSH consultancies are a likely service competitor (not checked).
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Under the OSH Act (Cap. 231), anyone using premises as a workplace must register it with the MGLSD Commissioner, and doing so without a certificate is an offence. A ministry speech and a law firm say the certificate is renewable every 3 years. The OSH (Amendment) Act No. 20 of 2025 took effect on 25 July 2025 and removed the 20-employee threshold, so all workplaces are now covered. However, registration itself is filed through the free state portal OSHMIS (oshmis.mglsd.go.ug), so the software would be selling only the record-keeping and amendment compliance pack. I found no commercial Ugandan OSH software, only a UNCST prototype and Kashari Consults (in development). Weaknesses: most firms are informal, enforcement looks weak, willingness to pay is low, and no lift or boiler inspection schedule was confirmed.

challenge_check.killer: None confirmed. The free OSHMIS portal (oshmis.mglsd.go.ug) covers the registration step, and weak inspection capacity (EPRC 2026: 1 inspector per 486,421 workers) limits pressure to comply.
challenge_check.reason: I found no product, rule or fact that kills this candidate, but it stays weak. The free state portal OSHMIS (relaunched at the 2025 OSH awards) already handles registration and certificates. The ministry also issues the incident register and inspection checklist itself. That leaves a private tool only the compliance pack layered on top. Demand got stronger: the OSH Amendment Act No. 20 of 2025 (in force 25 July 2025) removed the 20-employee threshold, so every workplace now owes duties such as a safety committee, a safety officer, audits and a health surveillance plan. Enforcement is the weak point. An EPRC study (September 2026) puts the inspector-to-worker ratio at 1:486,421, with fewer than half of workplaces inspected. The only local competitors I found are prototypes (UNCST, Kashari Consults). OSH consultancies are a likely service rival, but I didn't check them. How much small firms would pay is unverified.
